summary.text: 河 means “river,” with a historical association especially with the Yellow River. It combines a water component, 氵, with 可 as a sound cue. The two parts divide the work: water identifies the subject, while the other component helps explain how the character was read.

history.text: The Shuowen explicitly analyzes 河 as water plus the sound of 可. Wiktionary describes a more varied early history, including forms with 水 and 何 as well as 水 and 可. Its account therefore places the familiar construction within a family of early spellings, rather than tracing every form through one simple shape.

uncertainties.text: The detailed relationships among the early spellings rely on Wiktionary’s account; the cited passage does not present the inscriptions needed to assess those relationships directly. They should not be used to claim a single uninterrupted graphic sequence.
